newDescription:
In this Year 3 English lesson, pupils learn how main clauses and subordinate clauses work together, and how subordinating conjunctions help connect ideas in a sentence.

This lesson includes:
✔ Learning common subordinating conjunctions using the mnemonic 'I SAW A WABUB'
✔ Using conjunctions such as if, since, as, when, although, while, after, before, until and because
✔ Understanding that a main clause makes complete sense on its own
✔ Understanding that a subordinate clause depends on a main clause to make complete sense
✔ Identifying the main clause and subordinate clause in a sentence
✔ Recognising that subordinate clauses often begin with subordinating conjunctions
✔ Adding suitable main clauses to subordinate clause starters
✔ Adding subordinate clauses to simple sentences to give more detail
✔ Using subordinate clauses at the beginning or end of a sentence
✔ Using a comma after a subordinate clause when it comes at the beginning of a sentence
✔ Knowing that a comma is usually not needed when the subordinate clause comes at the end
✔ Extending simple sentences to make writing more detailed and interesting

Pupils begin by learning a set of common subordinating conjunctions and using them to complete sentences. They then compare main clauses with subordinate clauses and explore why a subordinate clause cannot usually stand alone.

The lesson develops through identification and sentence-building activities. Pupils spot subordinate clauses, add main clauses to clause starters and write their own sentence endings using appropriate subordinating conjunctions.

Later activities focus on position and punctuation. Pupils see how subordinate clauses can appear at the beginning or end of a sentence and practise using commas correctly when the subordinate clause comes first.

The final task asks pupils to extend simple sentences by adding subordinate clauses, helping them make their writing more informative and engaging.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify main and subordinate clauses, use subordinating conjunctions accurately, and extend sentences with correctly punctuated subordinate clauses.
